about.title: Calabasas Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Calabasas sits at the crossing point of the Ventura Freeway and canyon roads like Las Virgenes and Mulholland Highway, where commuter traffic, weekend riders, and local drivers all converge. Public records show 96 injury collisions in the most recent final year, with 132 people hurt and one traffic death — and Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. see a noticeable jump in reported crashes. Whether you were rear-ended on Calabasas Road or caught in freeway traffic near the 101, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster calling before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured drivers, passengers, and cyclists with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Our role is simply to make that first connection easier while you focus on getting better.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a Calabasas Crash

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — such as the county road authority — may be involved. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible, though your share of fault reduces the amount. Early evidence from Las Virgenes or Mulholland Highway can help establish an accurate picture before memories fade.

items.title: Avoid the Recorded Statement Trap
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash, and anything you say can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can speak on your behalf so you're not navigating that call alone.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a crash in Calabasas?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the accident to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government agency was involved — for example, a road defect on a county-maintained street — that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your situation early.

items.question: What if the crash happened on Las Virgenes Road or Mulholland Highway, where fault seems unclear?
items.answer: Canyon roads and multi-lane corridors like these can involve visibility issues, speed, or multiple vehicles, which sometimes muddies fault. California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you're found partially at fault, just reduced by your percentage of responsibility.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company first?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other side's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to reduce what they eventually offer, and an independent attorney can help protect your interests from the start.
